absent: Full inode lifecycle beyond the conditional reference attempt, including expiration coordination and filesystem clear handling.
Complete sysctl set translation, header lifetime and locking beyond directory creation, validation and unregister reconciliation shown.
Semantics of file operation callbacks and of security, async, owner and access helpers invoked during teardown.
Internals of poll unlinking, notification delivery, mount tree detachment and namespace lifetime beyond the triggers observed.
Generic lock conflict predicate, blocked waiter wakeup protocol and open file description lock handling beyond close time removal.
Filesystem registration and unregistration paths that mutate the list and advance the generation counter.
Sequence file buffer management beyond single append overflow reporting.
Allocation failure handling for directory objects beyond error propagation and diagnostic emission.

findings.text: igrab provides a safe attempt to hold an inode that might be expiring concurrently. Success returns the same object with an extra held reference, while an object already entering freeing yields null with no reference taken.

A new reference is granted only while freeing indicators remain clear. The path first attempts a conditional atomic increment with a state validation, and otherwise rechecks the same indicators under inode spin protection before incrementing, returning null when freeing is observed.

Sysctl directory creation resolves slash separated paths level by level, ignoring empty components and stopping with an error on allocation or insertion failure, otherwise returning the deepest directory reached with its usage count incremented.

Sysctl directory lookup and insertion serialize search, race revalidation and header linkage with global sysctl spin protection, releasing it only while allocating a fresh directory object and adjusting directory usage counts while protected.

A fresh control directory uses a single allocation holding a directory object, a node, one table entry and a trailing name copy. The entry carries the copied name with directory access attributes, and its header is bound to the owning set, root and node for a single entry.

Table registration validation requires every entry to carry a name and a handler, requires value handlers to supply both data and length with length consistency delegated to an array checker, and requires permission bits to stay within read write allowance for user group and other.

Single element vector handlers must declare a length matching their element width, with distinct widths for unsigned integer, byte and boolean forms, and byte range handlers must keep optional bound values within byte range.
Table check diagnostics record the enclosing path with the entry name and a formatted reason, and always contribute an invalid argument status that callers accumulate across entries.

Unregistration reconciliation for a non default set translates each parent directory to its core counterpart and looks up every registered name there, releasing matching directory pairs or root links and otherwise emitting a diagnostic that the expected peer is absent.

Two helpers allocate files without accounting. One builds an empty file from flags and credentials and marks it unaccounted, while the other first builds a pseudo path from name inode and mount, then attaches the path and operations and disables notification delivery by default.

Pseudo file creation forwards path construction failures directly, and when empty file allocation fails after path success it retains an inode reference before releasing the path to preserve lifetime balance.

Final file teardown for opened objects follows an ordered progression through notification, poll detachment, lock removal, security release, async and driver release, character device release for non path opens, operations and owner and access release, dentry and mount release with special dissolution handling, ending in object freeing. Unopened objects move directly to freeing.

Reference release is exposed through a work handler draining a lock free list, a callback wrapper recovering the file from task work, a flush routine draining both pending and scheduled work, and two synchronous helpers that run final teardown only when the last reference disappears.

Close time lock cleanup removes open file description locks, then flock locks, then leases, and finally verifies under context spin protection that no remaining entry of any family references the closing file, warning with device, inode and lock attributes when a leak is seen.

Close time flock removal builds an unlock request bound to the closing file as both file and owner, stamped with the caller thread group and marked with flock type, unbounded extent and close indication, delegating to driver handling when present and otherwise to the generic inode path before releasing private data.

Inode flock handling completes immediately when an entry for the same open file already carries the requested type, replaces it through a disposal list when types differ, and finishes unlocks after optional existence verification. Conflicting entries cause immediate failure for non sleeping requests or deferral through the blocked list for sleeping requests, while lack of conflict installs a copied lock and transfers waiters.
Two flock entries that share the same open file never conflict regardless of type, while entries for different files defer to the generic conflict predicate.

Flock mutation, lease removal and close verification hold a file wide read guard across context spin protection, with blocked waiter insertion additionally serialized by a global blocked spin protection.

Exhaustion during lock context or lock allocation fails acquisition with an out of memory indication, except plain unlock which still succeeds, while existence qualified unlock reports absence when no matching entry was found.

Mounts flagged for dissolution are handled on final file reference by first checking anonymous root status without blocking, then revalidating under exclusive namespace protection before detaching the tree and releasing namespace and mount references.

Anonymous root status holds only when the stored namespace pointer is valid and marked anonymous and its recorded root equals the examined mount, with the pointer obtained through a single atomic read.

Poll detachment on file release uses a fast unsynchronized observation to skip work when no poll linkage exists and otherwise delegates to full unlinking, with an alternate build providing an empty operation. Close notification chooses a write flavor when write access is present and a non write flavor otherwise before forwarding.

The cached filesystem listing pairs a deferred reclamation header with a generation counter, a length and a trailing character area. Global state combines a generation counter with a read mostly pointer to the current cache, with writers serialized by a dedicated spin lock.

The sysfs call multiplexes name to index resolution, indexed name copy with module reference protection, and total count reporting. Unknown selectors and failed lookups or copies yield invalid argument or fault indications as appropriate.

Registration list traversals for index, name, count, boot enumeration and proc display run under read side protection, while cache sizing, validation and publication run under the dedicated spin lock with generation checks and retry on concurrent change.

Boot time enumeration copies names of filesystems requiring block devices into a caller buffer as consecutive terminated strings, stopping with a warning when remaining space cannot hold the next name and returning how many names were stored.

Proc display prefers writing the cached string with its exact stored length into the sequence buffer, regenerating on cache absence by sizing, revalidating against concurrent regeneration or list change, populating one line per filesystem, publishing with deferred freeing of the predecessor, and falling back to direct iteration on allocation or consistency failure.
Sequence buffer append copies only when the resulting total stays strictly below capacity, otherwise it records overflow and reports failure without a partial copy.

Initialization creates a permanent proc entry for the filesystem listing bound to the cached display routine and reports allocation failure when creation fails. Single entry creation and permanence handling vary by build, with one configuration forwarding to a data variant, another yielding null, and permanence acting only with built in proc support.

Several failure paths only emit diagnostics and continue with the next item, including missing unregister peers, directory acquisition failures and leaked lock detection, each logging identifying context without further recovery.
Numeric selectors for the sysfs call are one for index lookup, two for name lookup and three for count query.
Allowed permission bits for sysctl entries are read and write for user group and other, and newly created control directories carry directory type with read and execute for user group and other.

Each line of the filesystems proc listing carries an optional nodev token followed by a tab separator, the registered name and a newline, while boot block device enumeration uses consecutive terminated names.
